Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators — overall risk: info.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • hatch_build.py contains a Hatch build hook (CustomBuildHook.initialize) that runs npm install and npm run build when building from source if web/dist is absent and web/package.json exists.
  • This appears intended to bundle the React frontend into the Python package. Based on the provided evidence, it is not tied to credential theft, a stealth loader, C2 communication, or other malware-like supply-chain behavior.
  • No .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, setup.py install-time payload, or interpreter-startup execution evidence was identified.
  • Ordinary console_scripts/CLI entry points require user invocation and were not treated as malicious automatic execution evidence.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • Credential-related names such as GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, and OAuth client secrets appear to be documented configuration for GitHub/GitLab integration and PAT/OAuth authentication.
  • Use of gh auth token and glab config get token is documented as a forge API authentication fallback. There is no evidence of broad environment harvesting, .env/SSH/cloud/CI token discovery, wallet collection, or key-file scraping.
  • GitHub/GitLab API and LLM API access are expected for the package’s stated functionality. No attacker-controlled C2, webhook exfiltration, paste/drop service, or raw-IP upload endpoint was identified.
  • No evidence of archive staging, temporary harvested bundles, base64/gzip/marshal/eval/exec loaders, or self-deleting droppers was identified.
  • No persistence evidence such as systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, or shell profile modification was identified.
  • No Kubernetes service-account abuse, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection evidence was identified.
  • cryptography/AES-GCM usage appears related to encrypting stored server OAuth/PAT tokens, not hiding an encrypted malicious payload.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • From the provided manifest and file contents, no hidden payload, unexplained native binary, typosquatting evidence, attacker-controlled domain, or wheel/sdist behavior mismatch was identified.
  • web/package-lock.json and numerous npm tarball URLs appear to be normal frontend dependency lockfile entries and are not by themselves malicious supply-chain evidence.
  • The hatch_build.py npm install/build step increases supply-chain exposure during source builds, but the provided evidence does not show malicious insertion or intentional credential theft.

Additional Verification Needed

  • Only selected text from 184 files was provided. web/package.json scripts, the full Python source tree, and the remainder of build configuration should be reviewed.
  • Compare the PyPI sdist against the upstream GitHub source, and inspect any separately published wheel for sdist/wheel mismatch.
  • Confirm from the full pyproject.toml whether the hatch_build.py build hook is actually enabled.
